The second passage describes the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882, which specifically targeted Chinese laborers.  
In the mid-to-late 19th century, Chinese immigrants came to the United States in large numbers, initially drawn by the California Gold Rush starting in 1848.  
Although many later worked on the transcontinental railroad, the first major wave was driven by gold mining, which created demand for labor and sparked migration to the West.  
This initial surge and the resulting nativist backlash were key factors leading to the 1882 law.
